svg.title: Owen A. Hurtado | Scientific Computing
svg.desc: Physics undergraduate exploring computation, numerical methods and astrophysics. The Flamm paraboloid represents an equatorial spatial slice outside a Schwarzschild black hole's event horizon. The meridians show a 30-second axial rotation of the 3D visualization, with directional lighting; this does not represent a rotating black hole. The equations and circular sections remain fixed. Occasional particle trails include four corner crossings and seven varied angles. Near the black hole, a subtle artistic deflection evokes gravitational lensing rather than a physical simulation; their timing is deterministic.

g.aria-label: Schwarzschild radius r sub s equals two G M over c squared. Embedding height z squared equals four r sub s times r minus r sub s.
